A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the multi-element isotopic fingerprint of lichens, associated with a land use-based sampling strategy, may be a relevant and efficient method for conducting biomonitorings studies to identify and characterize atmospheric contamination sources.
the multi-isotopic approach associated to a land-use characteristic based sampling strategy can be used to assess the spatial extent of contamination sources in an area.
a combination of isotopic signatures (Pb, Hg, δ15N, δC) and land use information may be used to identify and discriminate the main sources of atmospheric contamination.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the combination of the isotopic signatures of Pb and Hg in epiphytic organisms with the isotopic signatures for C and N may provide a powerful tool to better assess the atmospheric contamination inputs.
a combination of isotopic signatures in lichens can be a powerful approach to discriminate atmospheric inputs and to better assess the spatial extent of pollution sources.
the multi-elemental isotopes approach, associated with a GIS-based sampling strategy, may be a useful tool to better constrain atmospheric inputs and sources of pollution in a region.
